URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cx21en4807wo
TITLE: Andy Burnham pledges not to 're-run' Brexit arguments
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-18 10:02 (updated 17:03)
AUTHORS: Richard Wheeler, Kate Whannel
SOURCE: BBC News

KEY POINTS — BURNHAM LEEDS CONFERENCE SPEECH:
- "My view is that Brexit has been damaging, but I also believe the last thing we should do right now is re-run those arguments"
- "I am not proposing that the UK considers rejoining the EU"
- "I respect the decision that was made at the referendum and it is going to undermine everything I have said about strengthening democracy if we don't respect that vote"
- Pitch: vote for him was a vote to "change Labour"
- Called for transfer of money and resources from "a bloated national state" to "a malnourished local one"
- "We have hollowed out councils and have created an unaccountable state, where too much is delivered by outsourced agencies outside local councillors' control"
- "Labour needs to change if we are to regain people's trust"
- Country needs "serious rewiring"

STARMER:
- Asked if would set timetable for departure if Burnham wins Makerfield: "I'm not going to do that"
- Said Makerfield by-election was "a fight between Labour and Reform" — "I will be backing 100% whoever the [Labour] candidate is"
- Repeated insistence he would "not walk away" from the job of prime minister
- Wants to fight next general election but recognises "we've got to turn things" after dire 7 May election results
- 5 ministers resigned over Starmer's leadership following the results

LIB DEMS:
- Accused Burnham of "U-turning before he's even been elected" over Brexit stance

CONTEXT:
- Makerfield voted strongly for Brexit in 2016
- Labour won Makerfield 2024 with majority of 5,399 over Reform UK
- Reform won ~50% of vote share in area at local elections
- Farage: Reform "will throw absolutely everything at" the by-election
- Burnham said September 2025 he wanted to see UK back in EU within lifetime
